common_middle: The morning was busy in the small town. At the bakery, a child counted six loaves while the baker swept flour from the wooden counter. Across the street, two neighbors carried a heavy basket of pears to the market. A bird landed on the fence, watched the neighbors, and flew away when the bell rang. In the garden behind the library, a little dog dug a shallow hole but found only a smooth stone. The librarian put the stone in a box and asked the children to wash their hands before touching the books. After lunch, a light rain began. The shopkeeper closed the windows so the paper signs would not get wet. A boy helped his friend move three chairs away from the door. They talked about the clouds, the flowers by the gate, and the path that led past the pond. When the rain ended, the children walked slowly back to the square. The baker had already taken the bread from the oven, and the neighbors were still arranging fruit. Nobody changed the object they had put away earlier; the different people kept doing their own jobs. The clock sounded twice, and everyone remembered that they still had one last errand to finish before going home. They met under the tree beside the path, looked at the dry road, and tried to remember what had happened at the beginning of the day.
